name: Rigatoni alla Vodka
blurb: Rigatoni in a silky tomato-cream sauce sharpened with a splash of vodka and chilli.
method: Soften the shallot and chilli in the butter, fry the purée for 3 minutes.
Add the vodka and cook off, then the cream.
Toss the cooked rigatoni through with Parmesan and pasta water.

name: Orecchiette with Sausage & Broccoli
blurb: Fennel sausage crumbled through orecchiette with broccoli, garlic and chilli.
method: Boil the pasta, adding the broccoli for the last 4 minutes.
Fry the sausagemeat in the oil with the garlic and chilli until crisp.
Toss the drained pasta and broccoli through, mashing some broccoli in.

name: Bucatini all'Amatriciana
blurb: Guanciale, tomato, pecorino and chilli clinging to hollow bucatini. A Roman staple.
method: Render the guanciale until crisp, remove some for topping.
Add the wine, then the tomatoes and chilli and simmer 12 minutes.
Toss the pasta through with pecorino and the reserved crisp bits.

name: Lamb Ragù Pappardelle
blurb: Slow lamb shoulder ragù with rosemary and red wine over wide ribbons of pappardelle.
method: Brown the lamb, soften the soffritto, add the wine and reduce.
Add the tomatoes, stock and rosemary and braise 2 hours until falling apart, then shred.
Toss with the pasta and plenty of Parmesan.

name: Spaghetti Puttanesca
blurb: A gutsy sauce of tomatoes, olives, capers, anchovy and chilli. Pantry to plate in 20.
method: Melt the anchovies with the garlic and chilli in oil.
Add the tomatoes, olives and capers and simmer 12 minutes.
Toss with the spaghetti and parsley.

name: Stovetop Mac & Cheese
blurb: No oven — macaroni finished in an evaporated-milk and cheddar sauce until glossy. Fifteen minutes.
method: Cook the macaroni and drain, keeping a splash of water.
Return to the pan with the evaporated milk, cornflour and butter and warm.
Off the heat, stir in the cheddar and mustard until smooth.

name: Penne Arrabbiata
blurb: An angry little sauce of garlic, dried chilli and tomato. Fast, fiery, meat-free.
method: Gently fry the garlic and chilli in the oil until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes and simmer hard for 12 minutes.
Toss with the penne and parsley.

name: Creamy Mushroom Tagliatelle
blurb: Mixed mushrooms fried hard, deglazed with white wine and cream, tossed with tagliatelle.
method: Fry the mushrooms in oil until deep golden, add the shallot, garlic and thyme.
Add the wine and reduce, then the cream.
Toss the pasta through with Parmesan and pasta water.

name: Fettuccine Alfredo
blurb: Just butter, Parmesan and pasta water emulsified into a glossy cloak around fresh fettuccine.
method: Melt the butter with a ladle of pasta water in a wide pan.
Add the just-cooked pasta and toss.
Off the heat, add the Parmesan in handfuls, tossing hard to a creamy sauce; season with pepper.

name: Classic Beef Lasagne
blurb: Layers of slow beef ragù, béchamel and pasta baked until the edges frazzle. Feeds six.
method: Make a slow ragù with the mince, soffritto, milk and tomatoes, simmering 1 hour.
Make a béchamel with the butter, flour and milk.
Layer ragù, pasta and béchamel three times, top with cheese, bake at 190C for 40 minutes.

name: Spaghetti Aglio e Olio
blurb: Garlic sliced thin and gently fried in good oil with chilli, tossed with spaghetti and parsley.
method: Warm the oil with the garlic over low heat until pale gold, add the chilli.
Add the drained pasta and a splash of pasta water and toss.
Fold in the parsley and plenty of pepper.

name: Baked Ziti
blurb: Tubes of pasta in a herby tomato sauce with ricotta and mozzarella, baked bubbling. A family bake.
method: Simmer the tomatoes with the garlic and basil for 15 minutes.
Mix the cooked pasta with the sauce and ricotta, tip into a dish.
Top with torn mozzarella and Parmesan and bake at 190C for 25 minutes.

name: Spaghetti & Meatballs
blurb: Herby beef-and-pork meatballs simmered in tomato sauce over a tangle of spaghetti.
method: Mix the mince, breadcrumbs, egg and Parmesan and roll into balls, then brown.
Add the garlic and tomatoes and simmer 25 minutes.
Serve over spaghetti with basil and more Parmesan.

name: Spaghetti Carbonara
blurb: Guanciale, egg yolks, pecorino and black pepper — no cream, all technique.
method: Crisp the guanciale slowly; whisk the eggs with the pecorino and pepper.
Toss the hot drained pasta with the guanciale and its fat off the heat.
Add the egg mix, tossing and loosening with pasta water to a glossy sauce.

name: Salmon, Pea & Dill Penne
blurb: Flaked hot-smoked salmon, peas and dill folded through penne in a lemony crème fraîche.
method: Cook the penne, adding the peas for the last 3 minutes.
Off the heat, stir the crème fraîche, lemon, butter and dill into the drained pasta.
Fold in the salmon gently and loosen with pasta water.

name: Gnocchi alla Sorrentina
blurb: Gnocchi baked in tomato-basil sauce with pockets of melting mozzarella.
method: Simmer the tomatoes with the garlic and basil for 10 minutes.
Stir in the cooked gnocchi, tip into a dish, dot with mozzarella and Parmesan.
Bake at 200C for 15 minutes until bubbling.

name: Chilli Prawn Linguine
blurb: Prawns fried with garlic, chilli and cherry tomatoes, tossed with linguine, lemon and parsley.
method: Fry the garlic and chilli in the oil, add the tomatoes and squash a little.
Add the prawns and cook 2-3 minutes until pink.
Toss the linguine through with lemon, parsley and pasta water.

name: Cheesy Pasta Bake with Greens
blurb: Pasta and broccoli in a mustardy cheese sauce, crumbed and baked. A no-drama family bake.
method: Cook the pasta, adding the broccoli for the last 4 minutes.
Make a cheese sauce with the butter, flour, milk, cheddar and mustard.
Combine, top with breadcrumbs and bake at 200C for 20 minutes.

name: Tortellini in Brodo
blurb: Little filled pasta simmered in a clear, good chicken broth with Parmesan. Restorative, quick.
method: Bring the stock to a gentle simmer with the bay.
Drop in the tortellini and cook 3-4 minutes until they float and are tender.
Ladle into bowls with Parmesan, pepper and parsley.

name: Pesto Pasta with Beans & Potato
blurb: The Ligurian way — trofie with pesto, green beans and a few cubes of potato cooked in the pasta water.
method: Boil the pasta with the potato, adding the beans for the last 4 minutes.
Drain, keeping some water, and return to the pan.
Stir the pesto and Parmesan through, loosening with the reserved water.

name: Nduja Spaghetti with Burrata
blurb: A quick nduja-tomato sauce coating spaghetti, topped with a torn ball of cold burrata.
method: Melt the nduja with the garlic, add the passata and simmer 10 minutes.
Toss the spaghetti through with pasta water.
Top each bowl with torn burrata and basil.

name: Pasta alla Genovese
blurb: Onions cooked down for hours with beef until sweet and jammy, stirred through pasta. Napoli's slow ragù.
method: Brown the beef, add the onions, carrot and celery and a splash of water.
Cook very low, stirring, for 3 hours until the onions collapse to a brown sauce and the beef shreds.
Add the wine near the end; toss with the pasta and Parmesan.

name: Tomato & Butter Spaghetti
blurb: Tinned tomatoes simmered with a whole onion and a lot of butter — Marcella's three-ingredient sauce.
method: Simmer the tomatoes, onion halves and butter very gently for 40 minutes, crushing the tomatoes.
Discard the onion (or eat it), season.
Toss with the spaghetti and serve with Parmesan.

name: Cavatelli with Cavolo Nero & Chilli
blurb: Little pasta dumplings with cavolo nero cooked soft in garlic, chilli and anchovy oil.
method: Boil the pasta, adding the cavolo nero for the last 5 minutes.
Melt the anchovies with the garlic and chilli in the oil.
Toss everything with pasta water and top with crunchy crumbs.

name: Creamy Sausage & Kale Gnocchi
blurb: Sausagemeat, kale and gnocchi in a fennel-scented cream. One pan, twenty-five minutes.
method: Fry the sausagemeat in chunks with the fennel and chilli until browned.
Add the gnocchi and a splash of water and cook 5 minutes.
Stir in the cream and kale, simmer to wilt, finish with Parmesan.

name: Tuna & Caper Fusilli
blurb: Store-cupboard tuna, capers, olives and tomato tossed with fusilli. A ten-minute win.
method: Fry the garlic, add the passata, olives and capers and simmer 8 minutes.
Flake in the tuna with its oil.
Toss with the fusilli and parsley.

name: Lemon Ricotta Spaghetti
blurb: Whipped ricotta loosened with pasta water and lemon into a light, creamy no-cook sauce.
method: Beat the ricotta with the lemon, Parmesan, oil and pepper.
Loosen with a few spoons of pasta water to a cream.
Toss the drained spaghetti through and finish with basil.

name: Rigatoni with Slow-Cooked Peppers
blurb: Peppers and onions stewed down for an hour into a sweet, silky sauce for rigatoni. Peperonata pasta.
method: Cook the peppers, onions and garlic in the oil, covered, on low for 45 minutes, then uncovered to jam down.
Add the vinegar and season.
Toss with the rigatoni and basil, and pasta water to loosen.

name: Sausage & Fennel Conchiglie
blurb: Shells that trap a rich sausage, fennel and tomato sauce with a hint of cream.
method: Fry the sausagemeat with the fennel bulb and seeds until browned.
Add the passata and simmer 12 minutes, then a splash of cream.
Toss with the shells and Parmesan.

name: Anchovy & Breadcrumb Spaghetti
blurb: Melted anchovy, garlic and chilli in oil, tossed with spaghetti and a shower of crunchy pangrattato.
method: Fry the breadcrumbs in some oil until golden, set aside.
Melt the anchovies with the garlic and chilli in more oil.
Toss the pasta through with pasta water and parsley, top with the crumbs.

name: Baked Tortellini Alfredo
blurb: Cheese tortellini folded into a quick Alfredo, topped with mozzarella and baked golden.
method: Make a béchamel with the butter, flour and milk, melt in the Parmesan and nutmeg.
Toss with the just-boiled tortellini, tip into a dish, top with mozzarella.
Bake at 200C for 18 minutes until bubbling; finish with parsley.

name: Pici Cacio e Pepe
blurb: Hand-rolled fat spaghetti with just pecorino, black pepper and starchy water. Tuscan minimalism.
method: Toast the pepper in a wide pan and add a ladle of pasta water.
Add the very al dente pasta with more water.
Off the heat, add the pecorino in handfuls, tossing hard until glossy.

name: Courgette Carbonara
blurb: Ribbons of courgette softened in oil stand in for guanciale in a lighter, greener carbonara.
method: Fry the courgettes in oil with the garlic until soft and lightly golden.
Whisk the yolks with the pecorino and pepper.
Toss the hot pasta with the courgettes, then the egg mix off the heat with pasta water.

name: Linguine with Walnut Sauce
blurb: A creamy Ligurian salsa di noci — blitzed walnuts, bread, garlic and milk — over linguine.
ingredients: 1 slice white bread, soaked in milk
method: Blitz the walnuts, squeezed bread, garlic, milk, Parmesan and oil to a loose paste.
Loosen with pasta water to a pourable sauce.
Toss with the linguine and a little more Parmesan.

name: Store-Cupboard Spaghetti Vongole
blurb: Tinned clams, garlic, chilli and white wine make a very fast vongole when fresh ones aren't around.
method: Fry the garlic and chilli in the oil, add the wine and clam liquor and reduce.
Add the clams to warm through.
Toss the pasta through with parsley and a little pasta water.

name: Buffalo Chicken Mac & Cheese
blurb: Shredded hot-sauce chicken folded into a blue-cheese-spiked mac and baked with a crumb.
method: Toss the chicken in the hot sauce.
Make a cheese sauce, fold in the pasta, chicken and blue cheese.
Top with crumbs and bake at 200C for 20 minutes.

name: One-Pan Tomato & Feta Orzo
blurb: Orzo cooked risotto-style in a tomato base, finished with feta and dill. Twenty-five minutes, one pan.
method: Soften the shallot, add the orzo and toast for a minute.
Add the passata and stock and simmer, stirring, for 12 minutes until creamy.
Crumble over the feta and dill.

name: White Bolognese Tagliatelle
blurb: A tomato-free ragù of pork, veal and wine, enriched with milk and Parmesan. Subtle and rich.
method: Soften the soffritto, add the mince and brown gently without colouring too hard.
Add the wine, then the milk and nutmeg and let it cook away, then the stock.
Simmer 1 hour, toss with the pasta and Parmesan.

name: Pasta con le Sarde
blurb: The Sicilian classic — sardines, wild fennel, raisins, pine nuts and saffron through bucatini.
method: Soften the onion and chopped fennel with the saffron, add most of the sardines and break down.
Stir in the raisins and pine nuts, then the drained pasta and some water.
Top with the reserved sardines, fennel fronds and crunchy crumbs.

name: Gnocchi with Pesto & Peas
blurb: Boiled gnocchi and peas tossed with basil pesto and a little butter. Fifteen minutes, kid-approved.
method: Boil the gnocchi, adding the peas for the last 2 minutes.
Drain, keeping a splash of water, and return to the pan.
Stir the pesto, butter and Parmesan through, loosen with the water.

name: Chorizo & Tomato Spaghetti
blurb: Smoky chorizo crisped in the pan, its red oil enriching a quick tomato sauce for spaghetti.
method: Fry the chorizo until the oil runs, add the garlic and paprika.
Add the tomatoes and simmer 10 minutes.
Toss with the spaghetti, pasta water and parsley.

name: Lemon & Asparagus Linguine
blurb: Snapped asparagus cooked in the pasta water, tossed with linguine, lemon, mint and Parmesan.
method: Cook the linguine, adding the asparagus for the last 3 minutes.
Drain, keeping water, and return to the pan with the oil, lemon and Parmesan.
Loosen with pasta water and finish with mint and pepper.

name: Pasta alla Norma Bake
blurb: Rigatoni baked in a tomato and fried-aubergine sauce with ricotta salata. A generous Sicilian dish.
method: Fry the aubergine in oil until golden, drain.
Simmer the tomatoes with the garlic and basil, fold in the aubergine and cooked pasta.
Tip into a dish, crumble over the cheese and bake at 190C for 20 minutes.

name: Pancetta, Pea & Egg Spaghetti
blurb: A carbonara-adjacent quick pasta with sweet peas folded through the silky egg sauce.
method: Crisp the pancetta; whisk the yolks with the Parmesan and pepper.
Cook the pasta, adding the peas for the last 2 minutes.
Toss the hot pasta and peas with the pancetta, then the egg mix off the heat with pasta water.

name: Lobster Mac & Cheese
blurb: Chunks of lobster folded into a Gruyère-and-cheddar mac, baked with a buttery crumb. A special-occasion bowl.
method: Make a béchamel, melt in the cheeses and Dijon.
Fold in the pasta and most of the lobster, tip into a dish, scatter the rest of the lobster and the panko.
Bake at 200C for 20 minutes; finish with chives.

name: Marmite Spaghetti
blurb: Nigella's cult supper — spaghetti tossed in butter melted with Marmite and a little pasta water.
method: Melt the butter with the Marmite and pasta water in the pan.
Add the drained spaghetti and toss until glossy.
Serve with Parmesan.

name: Mushroom & Chestnut Tagliatelle
blurb: A woodsy autumn pasta of chestnut mushrooms, crumbled chestnuts, thyme and a splash of cream.
method: Fry the mushrooms until golden, add the shallot, chestnuts and thyme.
Add the cream and simmer 3 minutes.
Toss the pasta through with Parmesan and pasta water.
